scope_statement: Anatomy and attachments of the superficial MCL.
source_note: No sources were retrieved. The generation environment had no access to PubMed, Cochrane, any journal or any textbook. The Tier 1 source minimum is NOT met and this draft would not pass Tier 1 in the deployed pipeline. This is the first section on the site written entirely for professionals, and it is unverified.
claims_needing_verification: In front of the merge point the ligament is isolable; behind it, an injury is a corner injury.
The proximal tibial attachment is a dynamic coupling to semimembranosus, not just a second anchor.
Valgus restraint is shared, so laxity in extension means more than this ligament has failed.
The two tibial attachments split rotation restraint between external and internal.
Landmarks, not residual tissue, locate the attachments in a reconstruction.
